picks.matchup: New England Patriots vs Seattle Seahawks
picks.analysis: This is the Super Bowl rematch, but the number is what makes New England interesting. Seattle is a home favorite and enters the opener as defending champion, yet the Patriots get the valuable +3 while Drake Maye returns with A.J. Brown added to an offense that should be much more dangerous than last year's group. Seattle also opens with real uncertainty in the secondary: Ty Okada is out and Nick Emmanwori is questionable after ankle surgery. New England will miss TreVeyon Henderson, but the matchup still sets up well for a Patriots team that only needs to keep this within a field goal.

picks.analysis: Baltimore remains the preferred side at -3.5 because the Ravens have the biggest advantage where Week 1 games are often decided: quarterback and offensive continuity. Lamar Jackson enters another season as one of the league's most dangerous dual-threat quarterbacks, while Indianapolis hands Daniel Jones the reins in his first regular-season game back from last year's Achilles injury. The Colts should get Alec Pierce back, but they will also be without cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt due to suspension, leaving an important matchup against Lamar, Derrick Henry and Baltimore's explosive offense. With Baltimore favored by only 3.5, the Ravens have room to win a game that could separate late.

picks.matchup: Las Vegas Raiders vs Miami Dolphins
picks.analysis: Las Vegas is now the more convincing side at -3.5 because the quarterback mystery is gone: Kirk Cousins is officially the Raiders' Week 1 starter, with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza beginning the season as his backup. That experience gap matters against a Miami team entering a new era with Malik Willis at quarterback. The remaining swing factor is Ashton Jeanty's ankle, but Klint Kubiak remains optimistic that his starting back will be ready. Add home field and a veteran QB to a Raiders team trying to establish a new identity, and -3.5 offers a cleaner setup than it did when the line was smaller.

picks.matchup: Kansas City Chiefs vs Denver Broncos
picks.analysis: This is the game's biggest storyline and the number makes Denver especially interesting. Patrick Mahomes is expected to make his return nine months after tearing his ACL and LCL, but Kansas City is not getting a comfortable home number: the Chiefs are only -2.5 against the team that won the AFC West last season and has beaten Kansas City three straight times. Denver's defense already knows how to pressure Mahomes, while Kansas City could be without starting left tackle Josh Simmons because of a back injury. Mahomes' return makes the Chiefs dangerous, but at +2.5 the Broncos only need a one-score game to cash.

picks.analysis: The Steelers remain the side, but the reason has changed: Atlanta's quarterback uncertainty is over. The Falcons have officially named Tua Tagovailoa their Week 1 starter and Michael Penix Jr. will be inactive, while Aaron Rodgers gets a full veteran season-opening opportunity in Pittsburgh. That makes the matchup less about a QB competition and more about whether Tua can quickly settle into a new offense. Pittsburgh has home field, a veteran quarterback and the continuity of an offense built around Rodgers, giving the Steelers a solid path to cover the -3.

picks.matchup: Cincinnati Bengals vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers
picks.analysis: Cincinnati stays on the card at -4, but this is the pick with the biggest injury-related caution. Joe Burrow gives the Bengals the more established quarterback, and Cincinnati's offensive ceiling rises sharply when Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are together. Both receivers were limited early in Week 1 preparation, but Zac Taylor indicated they should be ready for the opener. Tampa Bay counters with Baker Mayfield and a strong offensive core of its own, so Cincinnati has to earn the cover rather than simply survive. The Bengals' home field and elite QB-WR combination give them the edge, but Chase and Higgins' final status should be monitored.
